transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, honestly, I'm just... I'm at my wit's end, really. What brings me in is I just cannot seem to keep my work in order anymore, and it's driving me absolutely crazy. I work at a dry cleaners, you see, and I've always had a lot on my plate there, but lately it's just become this complete disaster area. 

I stand there behind the counter, and I've got the claim tickets—you know, the
Did you have trouble with attention or staying organized when you were a child?

Oh! Well, yes. Oh boy, did I ever. I mean, it's funny you ask that because my mother used to keep all my old report cards in this big heavy cedar chest at the foot of her bed, and I was looking through them a while back. It was just... it was exactly the same story every single year, right from the beginning. 

Even way back in grade school—
Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energized or wired for several days in a row?

Energized? Wired for days? Oh, heavens no. I mean... honestly, I wish I did sometimes! Working at the dry cleaners, you know, it just drains it right out of you. You're standing on those hard linoleum floors all day long—eight, sometimes nine hours if we're short-staffed, which we always seem to be lately because my manager, Gary, just cannot seem to keep anyone hired for the afternoon shift—and the heat from the presses in the back just completely saps whatever energy you might have woken up with. 

By the time I get home, I am just... I'm completely wiped out. I usually just collapse on the sofa with a cup of tea and try to watch Jeopardy, and half the time I'm nodding off before Final Jeopardy even comes on. So, no, I've never had anything like that where I'm just buzzing along for days on end. I might get a little burst of energy if I have a second cup of coffee on a busy Tuesday morning, but that
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind even when you try to ignore them?
Unwanted thoughts? Like... things that just pop in and I can't get rid of them? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, my mind is definitely always going, just
Do these attention and organization problems happen outside of work too?
Oh, everywhere. It’s not just at the dry cleaners, though Lord knows it’s bad enough there. I mean, at the shop, it's been a real
Have these attention and organization problems caused serious problems in your daily life?

Well, yes, I suppose they have. At the shop, it's been a real mess lately. I mean, we've had late orders because I just lose track of which tickets go with which garments, especially when it gets busy and Gary is yelling from the back. And the billing—oh, don't get me started on the billing. I've gotten the numbers jumbled up more times than I can count, and it leads to these incredibly tense moments with the customers. You know, Mrs. Higgins came in last Tuesday, and I accidentally charged her for someone else's suede jacket cleaning, and she was just furious, understandably so, but it just made my stomach tie in knots. And the other girls at the counter get so frustrated with me when they have to fix my mistakes. It’s just awful. 

And it’s not just work, either. At church, I used to love helping out with the potluck committee and organizing the spring bazaar. I really did. But I had to step back from leading the planning this year. I was supposed to be in charge of coordinating the volunteers, and I kept forgetting to call people back, or I'd lose the sign-up sheet, and people were getting so annoyed with me. Pastor Dave was very sweet about it, but I could tell he was exasperated when the tablecloths didn't show up on time because I forgot to confirm the rental. It just feels like I'm letting everyone down, everywhere I go, because I just can't seem to keep it all straight in my head.
Have you had a head injury or other neurological illness?

A head injury? Oh, goodness, no. I mean, I've bumped my head on the racks at the cleaners—those metal bars hanging down from the conveyor can be a real menace if you're rushing, and I'm always rushing around trying to find things or catch up. Just last month I stood up too fast under the track and gave myself a pretty good whack, and Gary came out from the back and asked if I needed to sit down, but it was really just a bump. Nothing serious, no concussions or hospital visits or anything like that. I didn't even need an aspirin, really, it just stung for a minute.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things?
Worrying excessively? No, I wouldn't really say I'm a worrier. I mean, my sister Brenda, now she is a worrier. She watches the evening news
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

Feeling down? Well, no, not really. I mean, I get frustrated, certainly. Like I was saying about the shop and the church, it's just so aggravating when I mess things up, and I do feel bad about letting people down. I'll have moments where I think, "Oh, why can't I just get my act together?" and I might shed a tear out of sheer frustration when I can't find my keys for the third time in a week and I'm already late for my shift. But it's not a sad feeling, if that makes sense? It's not like a dark cloud hanging over me or feeling hopeless about life. I still love going to my Tuesday night bingo with the girls, and I get so excited when my grandkids come over on Sundays. We always make pancakes—blueberry for little Tommy and chocolate chip for Sarah—and I just love it. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm depressed. Just... overwhelmed and scattered, mostly. I just wish I could be more organized so I wouldn't have to feel so flustered all the time, you know? But no, not depressed.
